executive_assessment.text: Barekot and Nalgad add concrete warning-system and implementation constraints, alongside gender-differentiated livelihood vulnerability.
Thame and Madhesh illustrate different 2024 hazards and impacts; the evolving national totals and attribution statements retain their source-specific dates and uncertainty.
Flood displacement raised protection concerns, while named local recovery deployments and cash activities are outputs or plans, not evaluated effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: UNDP says climate-related floods, landslides and agricultural shifts threaten human security in Barekot and Nalgad, where over 90% rely on agriculture; gender inequalities heighten women's food, health and economic insecurity.
UNDP's local baseline found no formal early-warning systems in Barekot/Nalgad, poor warning awareness/access, and funding/technical barriers to implementing local plans.

The May 2025 NDC records flooding at Thame in August 2024 from two glacial-lake outbursts and separately identifies 47 potentially dangerous glacial lakes nationally; no event-specific attribution is claimed.

Source dated 2024-10-07 reports: The plan reports 21 affected districts and 246 deaths; 46,569 ha of Madhesh farmland were damaged, with crop losses expected to worsen food insecurity and negative coping.

UNDP's 5 January 2025 update reports ten community volunteers deployed in Namobuddha, Roshi, Timal, Bethanchock, Rajpur and Phidim to support shelter-data collection and access to government assistance.
As of 5 January 2025, cash support in Roshi/Namobuddha for 260 households and debris clearance were ongoing; a separate 600-household cash-for-work activity in Kavre/Lalitpur remained planned.

known_gaps.text: No inspected Nepal source explicitly links climate hazards to conflict or violence; no climate-FCV pathway is asserted.
The exposure and projection results are spatial or modeled estimates and should not be read as observed household-level losses.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The opened reports establish climate-related human-security, protection and livelihood pathways, but not a climate-to-armed-conflict causal link or conflict-driven adaptation constraint.
The UNDP local assessment covers two Jajarkot municipalities only; the 2024 flood-plan totals are preliminary, with limited district-level disaggregation.
The 7 October 2024 response plan and May 2025 NDC report different flood death and displacement totals/units; both are retained with their dates and sources, not reconciled.
UNDP recovery updates report deployment and ongoing/planned activities, not independent outcomes. The 2025 NDC does not identify the cited September 2024 event-attribution study.
Local human-security findings should not be converted into a conflict label. The assessed two municipalities and the 2024 flood-affected districts are distinct evidence scopes.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
